posts.note: Interview with NeuroSigma CEO Colin Keeley about the Monarch eTNS device. Most forecasts belong to the guest (a soon-to-be-announced two-hour evening trial; expansion to other neurodevelopmental disorders); only the author's restatement, one leading question, and the RAMHT event notice are logged.
Historical essay on the malaria cure and the lobotomy; normative calls for higher treatment standards not logged. Only the RAMHT event notice is forward-looking.
Methods-reading tutorial; generic replication truisms not logged. Only the RAMHT event notice is forward-looking.
Announcement of RAMHT New Orleans, September 14th; all statements are own-organization event plans.
Essay on psychedelic clinic economics; several present-tense claims about not-yet-approved drugs logged as borderline.
RAMHT New Orleans preview and interview with co-founder Grady Hannah; guest forecasts (LSD treatment 'coming soon') not logged as the author's.
Podcast blurb and donation appeal; no forward-looking claims.
Author's public comment to FDA docket FDA-2026-N-7542 on psychedelic access and reimbursement; dense with hedged and conditional calls. Pure recommendations ('should') not logged.
Short video post; only the RAMHT event date is forward-looking.

statements.quote: Right now the label says you wear it overnight, and you are looking at future studies on wearing it during the evening to see how much you actually need.
statements.context: Author's closing summary to NeuroSigma CEO Colin Keeley about the second-generation Monarch eTNS device for pediatric ADHD; restates Keeley's plan to study two-hour evening use instead of the eight-hour overnight paradigm. Keeley confirms with 'Yep'.
statements.note: Restatement for confirmation of Keeley's own forecast: 'we think we will soon announce a clinical trial where people would use the device for two hours in the evening'. Author checks rather than adopts.

statements.quote: So it may be that for children who are likely to find this treatment helpful, EEG could give us a signature letting us know that is the case?
statements.context: Author's leading question after Keeley describes the right-prefrontal EEG power increase as a candidate biomarker to predict and track response to Monarch eTNS in ADHD. Keeley answers 'That would be the ideal'.
statements.note: Phrased as a question to the interviewee; borderline. Logged for recall as a hedged expectation that EEG becomes a response biomarker.

statements.quote: Speakers who’ll help us explore a range of advancements in rapid acting mental health treatments include:
statements.context: Announces the speaker roster for RAMHT New Orleans: Jessica Malberg (Definium Therapeutics), Colleen Hanlon (BrainsWay), Andrew Penn (Salma Health), Kate Passanisi (CareNetGPO), Tobias Marton (Mindful Health Solutions), Steve Beller (Neurorelief), Kazu Okuda (Universal Brain), Jay Pathmanathan (Beacon Biosignals), Prantik Kundu (EyeThree).

statements.quote: We’ll be sharing more details on speakers, rapid-fire talks and panel discussions on the RAMHT website and LinkedIn page (follow us if you’re not!).
statements.context: Plan to publish further RAMHT New Orleans event details on the RAMHT website and LinkedIn page.

statements.quote: Also, we will have special guests. And surprises. And maybe….just maybe… embarrassing merch, for me, personally.
statements.context: Teaser for the RAMHT New Orleans event: special guests, surprises, and possibly embarrassing merchandise featuring the author.
statements.note: Own-event teaser; the merch part is jokey in tone but reads as a real plan.

statements.quote: pharmaceutical and device companies will only keep creating miracles if they make a hell of a lot of money doing it.
statements.context: Opening premise of the essay: continued innovation by pharmaceutical and device companies depends on large profits; sets up the argument that doctors should capture part of the psychedelic treatment economics.
statements.note: General conditional premise; borderline truism.

statements.quote: Now the squeeze. Drug prices go up every year. Physician reimbursement, against inflation, goes down every year.
statements.context: Buy-and-bill economics for Spravato (esketamine): the author asserts a continuing trend of rising drug prices and falling real physician reimbursement, so the doctor buys an increasingly expensive drug and gets paid a shrinking amount to administer it.
statements.note: Habitual-present trend claim that implies continuation; borderline.

statements.quote: The pipeline drugs behind Spravato — psilocybin, LSD, MDMA — will almost all require longer monitoring than we can currently bill
statements.context: 'The leverage' section: pipeline psychedelics will need in-clinic monitoring longer than current billing allows (the author earlier notes the prolonged-service code ceiling makes billing stop working past about two hours).
statements.note: First half of a compound sentence; the retail-pharmacy half is logged separately.

statements.quote: and none of them will go through a retail pharmacy.
statements.context: Same sentence as the monitoring claim: the pipeline psychedelics behind Spravato (psilocybin, LSD, MDMA) will not be dispensed through retail pharmacies; treatments are in-clinic by design.
statements.note: Second half of a compound sentence.

statements.quote: These treatments are in-clinic by design. The clinic is the distribution channel.
statements.context: Claim that pipeline psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, MDMA) will be delivered in clinics, making the clinic the distribution channel for the drugs.
statements.note: Present-tense restatement of the no-retail-pharmacy call about not-yet-approved drugs.

statements.quote: Those clinics need rooms — with cameras, IT infrastructure, furniture comfortable enough for a full day of treatment — and whoever pays for the rooms owns the economics.
statements.context: Claim that whoever funds psychedelic clinic infrastructure will capture the economics; the author names two candidates, physicians or the conglomerates acquiring them.
statements.note: General claim about future value capture; borderline.

statements.quote: For the first time in my career, the drug can’t get to the patient without us. That’s leverage. Pharma needs certified clinics the way it used to need a pharmacy’s shelf space.
statements.context: Claim that with psychedelics, pharmaceutical companies will depend on certified clinics and physicians as the scarce distribution resource.
statements.note: Present tense about not-yet-approved drugs; restated in my-open-comment-on-psychedelic-medicine.

statements.quote: We can stay terrible, and Optum and its colleagues will happily handle the details and pocket the dollars without us.
statements.context: Conditional: if doctors stay bad at business, Optum (UnitedHealth) and similar conglomerates will capture the psychedelic clinic economics.
statements.note: Conditional call.

statements.quote: I’d bet they’d prefer the set and setting of a clinic owned and operated by physicians
statements.context: Patients ('they') would prefer physician-owned psychedelic clinics over clinics run by insurer-owned companies.
statements.note: Preference claim; hard to resolve. Borderline.

statements.quote: The FDA is considering how psychedelics get regulated before any of them officially have been, and there’s an open comment period coming up on September 14th.
statements.context: P.S. of the essay: the FDA has an open public comment period on psychedelic regulation coming up on September 14th (the later post names docket FDA-2026-N-7542).
statements.note: Dated procedural call.

statements.quote: I’m gonna drop the un-Fable-edited version in a subsequent subscriber-only post and you can feel free to compare and agree with my wife.
statements.context: Editor's note: the author plans a subscriber-only post with the longer, unedited version of this essay.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise.

statements.quote: Speaker Colleen Hanlon, Ph.D. —who will be doing an “ask the expert” opening to the event
statements.context: News bullet on BrainsWay: Colleen Hanlon (VP Global Medical Affairs, BrainsWay) will open the RAMHT New Orleans event with an 'ask the expert' segment.

statements.quote: This is also the first RAMHT meeting with robust, shareable data: finally, top-line phase three data on lysergide D-tartrate, otherwise known as LSD, from Definium’s Emerge study in major depressive disorder and Voyage study in generalized anxiety disorder. For the first time we’ll know what double-blind, randomized controlled trials look like.
statements.context: Author tells RAMHT co-founder Grady Hannah that the upcoming New Orleans meeting will feature Definium's top-line phase 3 LSD (lysergide D-tartrate) data from the Emerge study in MDD and the Voyage study in GAD.
statements.note: Claim about own-event content; the trial data is described as already toplined.

statements.quote: It’s a whole different business. They’re there for hours in a row.
statements.context: Answer to Grady Hannah's question about how patients will be cared for during LSD treatment: the author expects LSD delivery to be a different business model with patients in clinic for hours; Grady adds 'And it's coming soon'.
statements.note: Present-tense description of a future treatment model; borderline. Grady's 'coming soon' is the guest's claim and is not logged.

statements.quote: I’m thrilled to say more soon, because we didn’t touch on novel diagnostic adjunctives: EEG and fMRI to understand what’s going on inside the brain before, during, and after these treatments.
statements.context: Author promises more content soon on EEG and fMRI diagnostic adjuncts for interventional psychiatry, ahead of the RAMHT event.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; trivial.

statements.quote: The pint-size Muir bobblehead is real, and prompt arrival enters you in the raffle.
statements.context: Event logistics: early attendees at RAMHT New Orleans enter a raffle for a limited edition Owen Muir bobblehead.
statements.note: Trivial own-event logistics; logged for recall.

statements.quote: The FDA is having another live meeting in which open comments on psychedelic medicines will be heard.
statements.context: Introduction: the FDA public hearing on docket FDA-2026-N-7542 ('Considerations for Potential Future Therapeutic Use of Psychedelic Drugs') will hear open public comments; the author contrasts it with the earlier MDMA-AT advisory committee.
statements.note: Procedural call about an announced FDA meeting.

statements.quote: The constraint on patient access to FDA-approved psychedelic therapies is likely to be financial.
statements.context: Summary of the author's comment to FDA: access to approved psychedelic therapies will be limited mainly by finances and reimbursement, not by supply.
statements.note: Thesis of the comment.

statements.quote: The supply chain that made oral drugs accessible is essentially not relevant to the deployment of psychedelic medicines.
statements.context: Summary: the pharmacy-benefit supply chain for oral drugs will not apply to the deployment of psychedelic medicines.
statements.note: Restates the no-retail-pharmacy call from cut-the-doctors-in-on-psychedelics.

statements.quote: The clinics that become the outpatient distribution centers become the “distribution channel” for these medicines
statements.context: Summary: clinics will be the distribution channel for psychedelic medicines; the sentence continues with the normative point that dispensing must be economically viable for individual clinics and large operators alike.
statements.note: Compound sentence; the normative second half is not logged.

statements.quote: the current “psychedelic therapy” category III codes only allow for up to 6 hours of total monitoring, which may not be enough for the programs you’re considering for some of these compounds.
statements.context: Section A: existing CPT category III psychedelic therapy codes cap monitoring at 6 hours, which the author expects may be insufficient for the REMS programs FDA is considering for some compounds.
statements.note: Hedged call.

statements.quote: The REMS program will drive the reimbursement infrastructure.
statements.context: Section A: the FDA REMS design for each psychedelic will determine how the reimbursement infrastructure is built.

statements.quote: The current reimbursement infrastructure used by ketamine is a workaround that didn’t involve creating a robust new code set, which will almost certainly need to be the case to encompass all the psychedelic treatments that are coming.
statements.context: Section A: a new billing code set will almost certainly be needed for the coming psychedelic treatments; ketamine's existing-code workaround will not scale.
statements.note: Also asserts that psychedelic treatments 'are coming'.

statements.quote: Nearly every psychedelic in late-stage development (psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, ibogaine, methylone and more ) all will need complexity based billing and longer monitoring–thanks to the longer acting effects compared to ketamine and esketamine– more similar to surgical procedures than current psychiatric practice.
statements.context: Section 2 (billing time limit of about two hours): late-stage psychedelics will need complexity-based billing and longer monitoring than ketamine and esketamine, more like surgical procedures.
statements.note: Restates the longer-monitoring call from cut-the-doctors-in-on-psychedelics.

statements.quote: It would be commercially and clinically disastrous for patients to have approved medicines that had no plausible means of reimbursement in the clinic itself
statements.context: Section 2: warning about the consequence if psychedelics are approved without a clinic reimbursement pathway.
statements.note: Conditional warning; borderline.

statements.quote: Waiting for post-approval rate negotiation, payer by payer and code by code, is itself an access barrier measured in years.
statements.context: Recommendation 3: payment pathways should be set concurrent with approval; if rate negotiation waits until after approval, access is delayed by years.
statements.note: Conditional consequence claim inside a recommendation.

statements.quote: It would also be acceptable to use the current category III codes for therapy and a G/J Code to account for the “buy-and-bill” activity ONLY, that is likely to be necessary.
statements.context: Recommendation 3: the author expects buy-and-bill (the clinic purchases and dispenses the drug) will likely be necessary for psychedelics.
statements.note: Hedged forecast embedded in a recommendation.

statements.quote: as well as the capital necessary to acquire what are likely to be expensive drugs.
statements.context: Recommendation 4: psychedelic drugs are expected to be expensive, so clinics will need capital to acquire them.

statements.quote: These rates need to take into account the fact that these drugs are likely to rise in price, and a drug price multiplier may need to be included in the calculation.
statements.context: Recommendation 4: psychedelic drug prices are expected to rise over time, so reimbursement rates may need a drug price multiplier.
statements.note: Normative frame with an embedded price forecast.

statements.quote: Coverage decisions will require economic data on the cost utility of these compounds
statements.context: Section 5: payers will require cost-utility data before covering psychedelics, in keeping with the TCET program and the not-yet-passed Breakthrough Treatments Act.

statements.quote: that would undercut financial support for these new treatments in the minds of financial markets, thus limiting future innovation.
statements.context: Section 6: if psychedelics repeat esketamine's years-long ramp to commercial viability, financial markets would withdraw support and future innovation would be limited.
statements.note: Conditional call built on the esketamine analogy.

statements.quote: What is acceptable according to Medicare is likely to be followed by other payors
statements.context: Section 6: private payers will likely follow Medicare's standards on prescriber type, training and certification for psychedelic treatments.

statements.quote: it may be teams of Psychiatrist and other health professionals, including other physician, practice types that may be involved in the dispensing of these medications.
statements.context: Section 6: the author expects psychedelic dispensing may involve teams of psychiatrists and other health professionals rather than psychiatrists alone.
statements.note: Hedged; embedded in a normative sentence about prescriber definitions.

statements.quote: A second out capable clinic will require dedicated treatment, per-patient rooms occupied for most of our working dayt, with monitoring personnel, secure, drug storage, compliant with rims and DEA requirements, audiovisual, and IT infrastructure for audit monitoring will also be required.
statements.context: Section C: forecast of what a psychedelic-capable clinic will require: per-patient rooms occupied most of the day, monitoring staff, secure drug storage compliant with REMS and DEA rules, audiovisual and IT infrastructure for audits. Source text contains typos ('dayt', 'rims').

statements.quote: If reimbursement does not count for them, the only entities able to observe the losses will be large, vertically, integrated organizations, the same organizations that have come under significant criticism recently.
statements.context: Section C: conditional: if reimbursement ignores clinic capital and operating costs, only large vertically integrated organizations will be able to absorb the losses.
statements.note: Conditional call.

statements.quote: Given set and setting are likely to be crucial factors of the deployment of these treatments
statements.context: Section C: the author expects set and setting to be crucial in the deployment of psychedelic treatments.
statements.note: Hedged and hard to resolve; borderline.

statements.quote: Independently owned, and physician lead practices are a bulwark against further inadvisable market consolidation, which these medications, rolled out without concern for the underlying economics, could make more common place.
statements.context: Section C: psychedelic medications rolled out without regard to clinic economics could accelerate market consolidation.
statements.note: Conditional call.

statements.quote: If the answer is no, access will narrow, regardless of how many products the FDA approves.
statements.context: Section C: if independent practices cannot deliver psychedelic treatments at payer rates without losing money, patient access will narrow despite FDA approvals.
statements.note: Conditional call.

statements.quote: Blanket in-person requirements across all phases of care would function as a geographic access restriction without a corresponding safety benefit.
statements.context: Section D (telehealth): if FDA requires in-person care for screening, preparation and follow-up as well as administration, it would restrict geographic access without a safety benefit.
statements.note: Conditional call.

statements.quote: For the first time in psychiatry, a class of medicines cannot reach patients without clinicians and clinical infrastructure in the loop.
statements.context: Conclusion: psychedelic medicines will require clinicians and clinical infrastructure to reach patients.
statements.note: Restatement of the leverage claim from cut-the-doctors-in-on-psychedelics.

statements.quote: That is an opportunity to build a delivery and payment system better aligned with patient outcomes than the rebate-driven pharmacy-benefit model it will not use anyway.
statements.context: Conclusion: psychedelic therapies will not use the rebate-driven pharmacy-benefit model.
statements.note: Restates the no-retail-pharmacy call.

statements.quote: they are the questions that will determine whether approved psychedelic therapies reach the patients the clinical trials were run for.
statements.context: Conclusion: reimbursement architecture, session-length billing ceilings and clinic-level economics will determine whether approved psychedelic therapies reach patients.

statements.quote: Our next live event is in September—on the 14th. 5pm in New Orleans.
statements.context: RAMHT's next live event: September 14th, 5pm, New Orleans (BK Historic House and Gardens).
